 respondent to pay compensation to the petitioner's land in survey No. 76

sentences.text:
This Writ Petition has been filed in the nature of Mandamus, seeking a direction to the second respondent/Special Revenue Divisional Officer / Land Acquisition Officer, Land Acquisition and Management Office, Madurai, to pay compensation for acquisition of the lands of the petitioner in survey No. 769/1C, totally measuring 2560 sq.ft in Balakrishnapuram Village, Dindigul East Taluk,
Dindigul District.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 2.The petitioner had filed L.A.O.P.No.44 of 2023 before the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Principal District Court, Dindigul questioning the very same award.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The land had been acquired,
compensation had been determined and award was also passed.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Questioning the Award in the manner known to law, the petitioner had filed land acquisition proceedings and it is pending.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The petitioner had also taken necessary steps in accordance with law.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: In that land proceedings, not only the petitioner herein, but also 15 other land owners are arrayed as petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: They are all joined together and filed the aforementioned L.A.O.P.No.44 of 2023.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 3.It is contended by the learned Additional Advocate General that the petitioner has not handed over the possession and is obstructing acquisition of land.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 4.The learned counsel for the petitioner stated that he is having two minor children, who require assistance owing to mental illness.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The respondents may consider that particular aspect.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
However,
the petitioner cannot stall the proceedings on that ground.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The petitioner had already initiated necessary procedure for that purpose.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5.Once compensation is fixed, award is passed, then the possession of land has to be handed over by the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The respondents are not the authorities to consider.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: So far as the children of the petitioner is concerned, the petitioner may seek relief independently before the appropriate authority, but not with the present respondents.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Before the Collector's Office, the petitioner tried to commit self-immolation.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The concerned Advocate is responsible for the conduct of the petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 7.It is made clear that any Advocate, who files vakalat for the client has not only to advise the client with the legal steps to be taken, but also prevent them from committing unlawful acts.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Threat to self-immolation is an unlawful act.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 8.The petitioner is directed to voluntarily hand over the land within a period of two weeks, from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, or else, the respondents may take necessary steps for possession of land in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis manner known to law.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The acquisition is for public welfare and social interest.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The petitioner must realise that he is also part of society and not living a solitary life.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 9.I am confident that the learned Principal District Judge, Dindigul would pass appropriate orders on considering all materials available on record.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 10.For the above reasons, this Writ Petition stands dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 8 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: For Appellant : Mr.V.Karuna  For Respondents : Mr.Veera Kathiravan  Additional Advocate General  JUDGMENT [Judgment of the Court was made by S.S.SUNDAR, J.]
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The appellant's property admittedly was acquired and the property also vested with the State Highways by virtue of Section 15(1) of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 2. The grievance of the appellant appears to be that the respondents acquired the land from his own brother.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Stating that higher compensation was paid to his brother's land and that the compensation fixed for the appellant's land is very low, the appellant filed a writ petition for a Mandamus to pay compensation to the appellant's land in Survey No.769/1C total extent 2560 sq.ft in Balakrishnapuram Village, Dindigul East Taluk, Dindigul District.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: . There is no dispute that the land belonged to the appellant was acquired after issuing a show cause notice and holding enquiry in accordance with the provisions of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is also admitted that notice under Section 15(1) of the Act was also issued.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The appellant's case is that he has not received the compensation and that therefore the acquisition proceedings cannot go further and his possession cannot be interfered with unless the compensation is paid to him.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 4. The learned Additional Advocate General, on instructions, submitted that the notification under Section 15(1) of the Tamilnadu Highways Act, 2001, was published on 16.05.2022 and that the land of the appellant vested with the Government free from all encumbrances on the publication of the said notification.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5. The learned Additional Advocate General then submitted that the appellant participated in the award proceedings and the compensation has also been determined by award enquiry in terms of Section 19(5) of the Act.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: He has also produced the records to show that the award enquiry notice was served on the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Since the appellant had not come forward to accept the compensation for his https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis acquired land, it is stated that a sum of Rs.4,57,982/- which S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113930487/
2 was fixed as compensation for the appellant's land, was deposited to the credit of LAOP.No.44/23 on the file of the Principal District Court, Dindigul, on 21.06.2023.
6.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: The grievance of the appellant is that the compensation fixed by the Land Acquisition Authority is inadequate.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is contended by the learned counsel for the appellant that the compensation fixed and disbursed to his brother is double the amount that was fixed in the case of the appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Therefore,
his case that the compensation is inadequate is established.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: In such circumstances, the remedy available to the appellant is to seek a reference in terms of Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 7. At this juncture, learned Additional Advocate General stated that the respondents made a reference for determining just compensation for the acquired land of the appellant and the said reference is also pending before the Principal District Court, Dindigul, under Section 77(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 8.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Therefore, this Court directs the Reference Court as well as the respondents to treat the reference not only as one under Section 77(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, but also under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013, so that the appellant may go before the learned Judge for getting higher compensation for his acquired land.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: 9. As per Section 15(1) read with Section 16 of the Tamilnadu Highways Act, 2001, the appellant's land vests with the Government free from encumbrance once a notification is published under Section 15 of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Assuming that the appellant has not been awarded compensation as determined by the authority under the Act, he cannot resist for handing over the possession of the acquired land to the respondents.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the prayer in the writ petition is misconceived.
sentences._hearing_file: S.Murugavel vs The District Collector on 7 August, 2023.json

sentences.text: Though the appellant is entitled to compensation, in view of the aforesaid direction to the Reference Court as well as the respondents to treat the reference not only under Section 77(2) but also under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, this appeal is dismissed.

sentences.text: It is open for the petitioner to move the reference court for payment out of the sum already deposited, pending further claim for enhancement of compensation.

opennyai_summary.final__facts: The appellant's property admittedly was acquired and the property also vested with the State Highways by virtue of Section 15(1) of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The appellant's case is that he has not received the compensation and that therefore the acquisition proceedings cannot go further and his possession cannot be interfered with unless the compensation is paid to him.
4. The learned Additional Advocate General, on instructions, submitted that the notification under Section 15(1) of the Tamilnadu Highways Act, 2001, was published on 16.05.2022 and that the land of the appellant vested with the Government free from all encumbrances on the publication of the said notification.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
Therefore, this Court directs the Reference Court as well as the respondents to treat the reference not only as one under Section 77(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, but also under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013, so that the appellant may go before the learned Judge for getting higher compensation for his acquired land.
Assuming that the appellant has not been awarded compensation as determined by the authority under the Act, he cannot resist for handing over the possession of the acquired land to the respondents.
Therefore, the prayer in the writ petition is misconceived.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
9. As per Section 15(1) read with Section 16 of the Tamilnadu Highways Act, 2001, the appellant's land vests with the Government free from encumbrance once a notification is published under Section 15 of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001.
Though the appellant is entitled to compensation, in view of the aforesaid direction to the Reference Court as well as the respondents to treat the reference not only under Section 77(2) but also under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, this appeal is dismissed.
It is open to the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondents to take possession of the property of the appellant which has been acquired in terms of Section 15 of the Tamil Nadu Highways Act, 2001.
It is open for the petitioner to move the reference court for payment out of the sum already deposited, pending further claim for enhancement of compensation.
Connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
